title: From Keser to Abba and Ima: the mazalos, the arms and netzach and hod of Arich Anpin
overview:
Having finished the *Keser*, the chapter shows how *chachma* and *bina*, *Abba* and *Ima*, receive from *Arich Anpin*, in three ways from highest to lowest. *Chachma* is the abstract point, an *ayin*, and *bina* the concrete explanation it shines into; behind the flash is the *koach hamaskil*.

Highest is the way of the *mazalos*, the beard: hairs in the membrane over the brain that drip its liquid, the first six as pleasure and the last six as intellect, *Abba* from the eighth and *Ima* from the thirteenth. The liquid is only leftovers, yet the hair is rooted in the skull, above the brain, like a sealed wineskin that leaks, or the nonsense of a mind under pressure, or the Torah as *novlos* of the wisdom above. So the thirteen attributes of mercy reach the sinner, and everything, even the Torah's sense, depends on the *mazal*. Lower, the intellect garbs the arms, the *middos* of the will, mountains of darkness: it rationalizes a bias like one bribed. Lowest, from *netzach* and *hod*, it is the everyday intellect on autopilot.

terms.gloss: a channel, from nozel, to drip; mazalos are the thirteen tufts of the beard of Arich Anpin, the hairs through which the brain's liquid drips
the eighth mazal, the source of chachma; its letters spell tzinor, a thin tube
the thirteenth mazal, the source of bina
the power of what: chachma's power to connect to something abstract, knowing it is there without understanding it
the hidden wisdom of Arich Anpin: the koach hamaskil, the source that brings out every intellect from nothing
the hidden brain: the liquid over the brain, the source of chachma, chachma of Keser
the skull: Keser of Keser, in which Atik is enclothed; the root of the hairs
leftovers, waste: what falls from a mind under pressure, whose root is higher than the intellect itself
the thirteen tufts of the beard, the thirteen attributes of mercy
the mountains of darkness: the middos of the will, feelings higher than the intellect could cause
the mountains of light: emotions that come from intellect and reason
the bribe: the love in the will that blinds the intellect and turns it to one side

sections.title: From Keser into Abba and Ima: three ways the intellect receives from Arich Anpin
sections.summary: Having finished the *Keser*, the chapter turns to the details of *Atzilus*: how *chachma* and *bina* (*Abba* and *Ima*) receive from *Arich Anpin*. There are three ways: from its *Nehi*, from its arms (*chesed* and *gevura*), and from its *mazalos*, the eighth and the thirteenth.

phrases.he: (כה) והנה מעתה יש להבין בפרטי ענין עשר ספירות דאצילות
phrases.en: Now we have to understand the details of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: Today's subject, he says, is the beard. With the *Keser* (crown) of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation) explained, now come the details of its ten *sefiros*: how the *Keser* is the source of *chachma* and *bina* (wisdom and understanding). Chapters 1 and 2 explained *Chabad*; here the book half skips it again, but shows how it goes from *Arich Anpin* (lit. the long countenance) to *Abba* and *Ima* (lit. father and mother; *chachma* and *bina* as *partzufim*): three ways the *sechel* (intellect) receives from the *Keser*.

phrases.he: דהיינו בירידת האור מחיצוניות נה''י דאריך אנפין באבא ואמא
phrases.en: That is, the way that the light from the *chitzoniyus* of *Nehi* of *Arich Anpin*, from the lowest level of *Arich Anpin*, descends into *Abba*, into *chachma* and *bina*, the *partzufim* of *chachma* and *bina*.

blocks.text: That is, how the light from the *chitzoniyus* (outer side) of *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*), the lowest level of *Arich Anpin*, descends into *Abba* and *Ima*. The first of the three ways: from the *Keser* through the *Chabad* and *Chagas* (*chesed*, *gevura*, *tiferes*) of *Atik* and *Arich*, down to *Nehi*, and the *Nehi* of *Arich* goes into *Abba*.

phrases.en: But sometimes we say

phrases.he: דאבא ואמא מלבישים לזרועות דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: that *Abba* and *Ima* garb, that they clothe the arms of *Arich Anpin*.
And that it says
the head of the king is fixed or dressed up in *chesed* and *gevura*:

phrases.he: היינו בחינת רישא דאריך אנפין דאתתקן בחסד וגבורה דעתיק יומין
phrases.en: that's talking about the way that the head of *Arich Anpin* connects to *chesed* and *gevura* of *Atik Yomin*.

phrases.he: חסד דעתיק יומין בגולגלתא כו' כנזכר לעיל)

blocks.text: Sometimes the *sechel* is said to receive not from *Nehi* but from the arms of *Arich Anpin*, which *Abba* and *Ima* garb, the right arm in *chachma* and the left in *bina*: "*Chachma* and *bina* are like puppets." The arms are *chesed* and *gevura* (kindness and might), the *middos* (emotional attributes) of *Chagas*; in this second way the *sechel* receives from *Chagas*.

A parenthesis: the *Zohar*'s *reisha d'malka b'chesed u'gevura istakan*, the head of the king is fixed, or dressed, in *chesed* and *gevura*, is not about this. It speaks of the head of *Arich Anpin* connecting to the *chesed* and *gevura* of *Atik Yomin* (lit. the Ancient of Days), a higher thing explained in chapter 21: the *chesed* of *Atik Yomin* becomes the *sechel*, its *gevura* the *mocha stima'a* (the hidden brain).

phrases.he: ולפעמים אומר דאבא יונק ממזל הח' ונוצר,
phrases.en: Sometimes we say that *Abba* and *Ima*, the *sechel*, receive from the *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*: that *Abba* receives from the eighth *mazal*, which is *v'notzer*,
and *Ima*, *bina*, receives from the thirteenth *mazal*, which is *v'nakeh*.

blocks.text: And sometimes *Abba* and *Ima* are said to receive from the *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin* (lit. flows; explained below): *Abba* from the eighth, *v'notzer*, *Ima* from the thirteenth, *v'nakeh*. The thirteen *mazalos* correspond to the *yud-gimmel middos harachamim*, the thirteen attributes of mercy.

sections.title: Chachma is ayin, bina is yesh: the flash and the koach hamaskil behind it
sections.summary: *Chachma* is the *koach MaH*, an abstract point grasped without understanding it, and *bina* is the concrete explanation it shines into: from nothing to something. The flash of *chachma* comes from the *koach hamaskil*, the hidden *chachma* of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.he: אך הנה ידוע בענין כח מה,
phrases.en: It's known about the idea of *koach MaH*, the power of what,
that *chachma* comes out from nothing, that the source of *chachma* is that it's an *ayin*.
And *bina* is called a *yesh*.

blocks.text: It is known about the *koach MaH* (the power of "what") that *chachma* comes from an *ayin* (nothing). It is the power to connect to something abstract, the *bittul* (self-nullification) of "what": you think about something you do not yet understand, know it is there, know nothing about it, and wonder, "What is it?"
So *chachma* is an *ayin*, and *bina* is called a *yesh* (something): you understand the thing in a tangible, concrete way and can explain it.

phrases.he: והאור ושפע דאין דחכמה מאיר ונמשך בבחינת השגה דבינה
phrases.en: And so this abstract point of *chachma*, this abstract understanding of the intangible point of an idea, shines into the understanding of *bina*.
That's the idea of going from an *ayin*, from a nothing, to *yesh*, to something; going from something abstract to something concrete.

blocks.text: The intangible point of *chachma* shines into the understanding of *bina*. The explanation holds what is beyond it, and so gives you more than itself: it anchors your perception of the abstract point.

blocks.title: The stick figure
blocks.text: That is why someone who gets it will get what you are saying, and someone who does not, won't. A stick figure barely resembles a person, but if you know what the original looks like, your mind conjures up the real thing. So *chachma* is enclothed in *bina*: the explanation is only a symbol that does not carry the whole idea, but the idea shines into it.

The explanation follows the idea, and in its words you can see the point: *chachma*, the abstract point, shines into *bina*, which makes it a concrete explanation, **from an ayin, from a nothing, to yesh, to something**.

phrases.he: ונקרא תרין רעין דלא מתפרשין כו',
phrases.en: And *chachma* and *bina* are called two friends that never part; they always work together.
And they dwell together.

blocks.text: *Chachma* and *bina* are *trein re'in d'lo misparshin*, two friends that never part, and *k'chada sharyan*, they dwell together: no *chachma* without *bina*, and no *bina* without *chachma*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת נקודה דחכמה שמבריק כברק מלמעלה מן השכל
phrases.en: And this is the idea of the flash of *chachma*: when you get an idea and a light bulb goes on over your head, and all of a sudden you get this idea, like a lightning bolt flashes in your mind.
And this is what the world calls understanding.

blocks.text: This is the flash of *chachma*: a light bulb goes on over your head, the idea flashes like a lightning bolt. Right away you start to develop it, analyze it and figure it out, and that is *bina*.

This flash is what the world calls understanding: "Oh, now I understand." They do not mean they can explain it, which is what this book calls *bina*. Tell someone a new idea and he catches the point; that is really *chachma*. He cannot explain it to anyone else, not even to himself; he just saw the point.

phrases.en: This comes from the *koach hamaskil*, the mind's power to bring out ideas, which is called the power of intellect.
And this is also called the *chachma stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*.
It's also called the hidden *chachma*,

phrases.he: שהוא מקור מוצא כל שכל מאין כו',
phrases.en: and this is the source that brings out every intellect; the idea is brought out from nothing.
And it's called *maskil*, the one that makes the intellect, the intellectualizer.

blocks.text: This lightning bolt comes from the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight), the mind's power to bring out ideas. In *sefiros* it is the *chachma stima'a* (hidden wisdom) of *Arich Anpin*, also called *chachma ne'elama*: the source that brings every intellect out of nothing, called the *maskil*, the one who makes the intellect.

sections.title: The mazalos: hairs in the brain's membrane that drip the source of pleasure and intellect
sections.summary: The thirteen *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*, the tufts of its beard, are channels through the membrane over the brain: the first six bring pleasure, the last six intellect. *Abba* suckles from the eighth, *v'notzer*, a thin tube, and *Ima* from the thirteenth, *v'nakeh*; the two are united in their source, so study in *bina* brings new flashes of *chachma*.

phrases.he: והיינו שאמר דאור אבא יונק ממזל הח', ונוצר
phrases.en: That *Abba*, *chachma*, suckles from the eighth *mazal*, which is *v'notzer*,
which is the letters of *tzinor*, like a pipe,
because it's like a thin tube.
And so this is the way of the hairs of this eighth *mazal*:

phrases.he: הוא בחינת צומח שבמשכיל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: this is the power of growth from this source of the intellect.

blocks.text: So *Abba*, *chachma*, suckles from the eighth *mazal*, *v'notzer*, which has the letters of *tzinor*, a pipe, a thin tube. The hairs of this *mazal* are the power of growth in the *maskil*, the source of intellect.

This is the beard of *Arich Anpin*, and it corresponds to the actual beard. Between the brain and the skull is the *kruma d'avira*, the membrane of air: spongy, full of a liquid that drips through tiny hairs into the brain. That liquid, it says, is the essential pleasure and also the essential power of intellect.

On the brain it is revealed as pleasure or as intellect, depending on where it comes out. The thirteen *mazalos* are thirteen ways through the membrane. The first six, on the side of *chesed*, let out a lot, and abundance causes pleasure; the last six, on the side of *gevura*, let out much less, and it comes out as intellect.

The first *mazal*, the most abundant, gives the most general pleasure; down through the six it grows more localized, to a *taanug murkav*, pleasure in a very specific thing. The last six are already intellect.

The first of those, the eighth, is the source of *chachma*: its brain is cold and wet, with more liquid, so its understanding is intuitive and holistic. *Bina* is dry and hot, very little liquid through very thin hairs, so it comes localized, a very specific intellect.
The middle, seventh *mazal*, *v'emes*, is the intermediary: it makes the *hachra'a* (decision) between *chesed* and *gevura*, so that the intellect is not only objective but decides and chooses.

*Mazal* is like *nozel*, to drip, and, he adds without vouching for the source, like the English "nozzle": a pipe, a tube. The stars are called *mazalos* because they are channels: the sun brings heat and light, and each star and planet affects the Earth in its own way.

So the *mazalos* of *Arich* are the channels that bring the liquid into the brain, bringing out pleasure and intellect. *V'notzer*, the source of *chachma*, is a *tzinor dak*, a thin tube; its hairs grow the intellect as the liquid comes out. From this brain comes the hidden *maskil*: a new idea first drips down as if from nowhere, then grows as it continues.

phrases.en: And this is the idea that it grows, it sprouts from nowhere, from nothing, all sorts of ideas.

phrases.he: והיניקה הוא בחינת הגדלת מוחין דאבא
phrases.en: And that the brain of *chachma* draws life, that it sucks from this *mazal*, is what causes the brain of *chachma* to develop and mature.

phrases.he: והגדלת מוחין דאימא, היינו ממזל הי''ג, ונקה
phrases.en: And the development of the brain of *Ima*, of *bina*, is from the thirteenth *mazal*, which is *v'nakeh*.

blocks.text: It sprouts all sorts of ideas from nothing. The suckling is the brain of *chachma* drawing this liquid, which develops the idea and matures the whole brain. The brain of *Ima*, *bina*, develops from the thirteenth *mazal*, *v'nakeh*.

phrases.he: וב' מזלות הללו, מזל העליון ומזל התחתון,
phrases.en: And these two *mazalos*, the highest and the lowest *mazal*,
they are the source for the intellect of *Abba* and *Ima*, of *chachma* and *bina*.
And this source is in the *koach hamaskil* itself.
So in this itself is a source for the development of the brain of understanding, which is, in the language of the world, *chachma*: just to get an idea.
And there's also the source for the development of the brain of grasp, to understand in a way that you can explain it, which is *bina*.

phrases.he: שהן נקראים מוח אבא ומוח אימא כידוע
phrases.en: These two brains are called the brain of *Abba*, the brain of the father, and the brain of the mother, *chachma* and *bina*, as is known.

blocks.text: These two are called the highest and the lowest *mazal* because they are the highest and lowest of the last six, those that relate to *sechel*. They are the roots of the intellect of *Abba* and *Ima*, *chachma* and *bina*.

This root is in the *koach hamaskil* itself. The liquid and the shape of the membrane over the brain are the source of your talents: the six of pleasure shape what you will enjoy and have aptitude and sensitivity for; the six of intellect, how your brain will work and what you will be good at.

Within this source is a root for the brain of understanding, in the world's language *chachma*, just getting an idea, and a root for the brain of grasp, understanding well enough to explain, which is *bina*. These are the brain of *Abba*, the father, and of *Ima*, the mother.

phrases.he: וכמו שבחינת מוח בינה שהוא מוח התפיסא וההשגה, מקבל מבחינת האין דמוח החכמה,
phrases.en: And just like in the revealed intellect, first you have an intuitive understanding in *chachma*, a holistic, abstract understanding of *chachma*, and then that understanding is developed and explained by the brain of *bina*,
so too in their source,

phrases.he: ביחוד ב' מזלות דאריך אנפין ונוצר ונקה כו'
phrases.en: with the unification of these two *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*, the *mazal* of *v'notzer* and the *mazal* of *v'nakeh*.

blocks.text: In the revealed intellect an intuitive, holistic understanding comes first in *chachma*, and then *bina* develops and explains it. So too in the source: through the union of the two *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*, the intellect goes from *v'notzer* to *v'nakeh*, and that is why below it starts in *chachma* and goes over to *bina*.

This is also why studying something in *bina*, doing *hisbonenus* (contemplation), brings new flashes of *chachma*: in their source the two are connected. Working in *bina* draws more liquid into *v'nakeh*, which automatically draws more into *v'notzer*, and out comes a new idea.

blocks.title: What modern science knows about the brain
blocks.text:
What does modern science say about the brain, this liquid and the membranes? Rabbi Walters has found nothing conclusive; they seem to be still researching it. So he explains it as the Torah sources do, without correlations.

Correlating Torah with medicine or science is tricky anyway: the terms differ, and science keeps producing new and contradictory theories. Sometimes the connection is obvious, sometimes possible, sometimes there is not enough. The *Zohar* has some seventy pages on the brain, its membranes and liquids; science, he has heard, having researched the liver and the heart, is only now starting on the brain. Maybe in ten or thirty years they will figure it out: "we'll have to wait and see."

sections.title: Leftovers from a higher source: the hairs, the sealed wineskin and novlos chachma
sections.summary: The hairs carry only the leftovers of the *mocha stima'a*, yet their root is the skull, higher than the brain itself, and that is why they burst out as waste. So too the nonsense that comes out of a mind under pressure, and the Torah, the *novlos* of the wisdom above: a thing forced down low reveals its essence.

phrases.en: And it's known
that even though these *mazalos* are called hairs,
the idea of a hair is that it bursts out of the skin and then it grows out:

phrases.he: רק מבחינת מותרי מוחא סתימאה דאריך אנפין,
phrases.en: they're growing only from the leftovers of the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*.
But their source is from the *atzmus hagulgalta*, from the actual skull itself.

blocks.text: The *mazalos* are called hairs. They connect to the hairs of the head and beard, but here they are the hairs inside the brain, from the membrane: that is the *mashal*, and above it is a kind of *tzimtzum* (contraction). A hair bursts out of the skin and grows; these grow only from the leftovers of the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*.

The hair has two parts. The tube itself is connected to *Keser*, the skull. The liquid dripping through it comes from the *mocha stima'a*, the hidden source of intellect, but only its leftovers, a little drop. Even so, their source is the *atzmus hagulgalta*, the skull itself.

phrases.en: Which is higher than this liquid.
Therefore
this is the reason why the hairs come out as leftover, or like a waste: because their source is so high.

blocks.text: The skull is higher than the liquid: the liquid is the source of *chachma*, *chachma* of *Keser*, while the *gulgalta* is *Keser* of *Keser*, where *Atik Yomin* is enclothed. Because their source is so high, the hairs come out as leftover, as waste. What is the *mashal*?

phrases.he: כמשל בקיעת הנוד סתום ביותר כו'
phrases.en: Like if you have a very tightly sealed wine skin or a water sack: if it's very full and very tight, some of it will seep through the pores, it will leak out a little bit.

blocks.title: The tightly sealed wineskin
blocks.text: A very full, tightly sealed wineskin or water sack: some of the liquid seeps through the pores. So the skull forms a tight seal that forces a few drops of the liquid through the membrane into the brain. Most stays on top of the brain; only the pressure forces some through.

phrases.he: כמו החכמה כשגובר עליו כח בשכל ביותר,
phrases.en: For example with your intellect: when somebody's really thinking hard, and the power of the intellect is really pressuring it,
so besides coming up with good ideas, they'll also come up with some ridiculous nonsense.

phrases.he: ששרש הנובלות יותר גבוה מגוף אור השכל
phrases.en: But actually the source of these jokes or this nonsense is higher than the intellect itself.

blocks.title: The think tank
blocks.text: So too with the intellect: when the power of the intellect presses, when someone thinks really hard, besides good ideas he comes up with ridiculous nonsense. Brainstorm in a think tank and you get a lot of good ideas and a lot of nonsense. That is *novlos*, the leftovers, the waste.

But the source of this nonsense is higher than the intellect: the level above it forces it down, and coming down so low shows a higher source. The intellect is not working on its own level; the *Keser* is pushing it.

That is why *shtus* (foolishness) higher than intellect looks like *shtus*: *shtus d'kedusha* (holy foolishness). Even in *kelipa*, *shtus* comes from the *ratzon* (will) forcing the intellect its way, and the intellect will produce whatever the *ratzon* tells it, "even if it's stupid."

blocks.question: Does this mean that whoever says stupid things is very smart?
blocks.text: No: saying stupid things does not make someone smart; he could just be saying stupid things. This is about *sichas chullin shel talmidei chachamim*, the everyday talk of Torah scholars. A *talmid chacham*'s jokes hide deeper wisdom than his Torah, because what is too deep to explain comes out in a joke, the *etzem* (essence) of the idea in a *levush zar* (a strange garment), like a *mashal* or a riddle. Regular people's *shtus* means only that they were not thinking hard.

Not a regular joke that is just nonsense, but things that seem very low and come from a high place, like the *Gemara*'s stories of the sages joking with each other, where a very big *chachma* is at work. Such low things are **higher than the intellect itself**, than the light of the *sechel*.

phrases.he: ולכך אמר דנובלות חכמה של מעלה תורה,
phrases.en: Therefore it says that the Torah is like the leftover waste of the *chachma* above, of G-d's wisdom.
And it says that this is a praise.
Like it's explained elsewhere.

blocks.text: Therefore the Torah is called *novlos chachma shel maala*, the leftover waste of G-d's wisdom, and *l'shevach davka*, specifically as praise, not as if it were nothing of His wisdom. G-d lowered His wisdom to tell us what to do with our cows, if one gores another, how to keep *Shabbos*, do business, eat, sleep, walk and dress: things that for the intellect would be *novlos*, petty, like garbage.

That the *sechel* comes down to that shows the whole *chachma*, of *Atzilus* and of *Adam Kadmon*, is only for us: Hashem's *etzem* chooses us down here, and that is its real purpose. In itself *chachma* is just *chachma*, not connected to the *etzem*; coming out as Torah, to make a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), it reveals His *etzem*. That is why the Torah is *davka* the greatest *chachma*, brought out by coming down very low.

One of the big rules of *Chassidus*: when something higher is forced down to a lower level, it has to reveal its *etzem*, which is above its level, and so in coming down it gains.

So if you want to really understand something, teach it: having to lower it and explain it simply forces you to understand it far deeper than learning it for yourself.

And bringing it out *l'maaseh*, as a practical *hora'a* (instruction), as a *Rav* who must *pasken* a *halacha* or a *mashpia* (mentor) advising someone what to do, reaches the *etzem* of the *sechel*, even more than teaching it. That is *lilmod al menas laasos*, learning in order to do.

He was just learning *Hemshech Samech Vav*, he says, but this rule is in *maamarim* all over. A *Rav* who has to *pasken* is afraid he will get it wrong: it is not a theory, he has to tell them the right thing. That fear gives him a deeper *bittul* to the idea than his pleasure in explaining it, and the deeper *bittul* reaches the *etzem*, which the enjoyment cannot.

That is a *Rav*'s advantage, but it holds for yourself too: learn *halacha* to know what to do in your house, or what to tell someone who asks. Even learning *Chassidus*, ask what it tells you to do: how to live differently than had you not learned it, how to act in this situation.

The Rebbe stressed this a lot: it is a *klal* in *Chassidus* and in Torah that even the highest ideas need a *hora'a l'poel*. Every *sicha* and *maamar* ends with a *hora'a l'maaseh*, a lesson in our *avoda*, because that is how you get to the *etzem* of the idea, as with the Torah being *novlos chachma shel maala*.

sections.title: Thirteen attributes of mercy and "everything depends on mazal": the Essence above reason
sections.summary: The thirteen attributes of mercy are the tufts of the beard: they reach the very low, our sins, and so show a connection higher than Torah and reason. So when *Abba* suckles from the *mazal* it receives from the essence of *Keser*, and even the *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal*, the union of *chachma* and *bina*, depends on the *mazal*: G-d decides what makes sense.

phrases.he: וכך הוא טעם מעלות ענין שרש י''ג מדות הרחמים
phrases.en: This is also the reason why the thirteen *middos harachamim* are so great,

phrases.he: שנקרא בשם י''ג תיקוני דיקנא כו',
phrases.en: and they're called the thirteen tufts of the beard.
The idea of the beard is that it comes out from the leftovers of the brain.

blocks.text: This is why the *yud-gimmel middos harachamim* (the thirteen attributes of mercy) are so great. They are called the *yud-gimmel tikunei dikna*, the thirteen tufts of the beard. The beard comes out of the brain's leftovers, but coming out to something so low shows that its source is very high.

The thirteen attributes are *davka* for when we sin, for very low things, and that Hashem connects to those shows a source higher than the Torah. That He forgives us, and even makes our *aveiros* (sins) into *mitzvos*, shows an essential connection, higher than a reason, higher than *sechel*.

phrases.en: Like it says,
*Hashem* passed over His face,
and He said, *Hashem*, *Hashem*.

blocks.text: As it says, *vaya'avor Hashem al panav vayikra Hashem Hashem*: when the thirteen attributes are said, Hashem passed over His face, past the *pnimiyus* (the inner side) and the *sechel*, to the *etzem*, and called, "*Hashem*, *Hashem*."

phrases.en: It reaches all the way up to the *etzem*, which is higher than the *mocha stima'a*, the source of the intellect,

phrases.he: שנקרא טעם וחכמה כמוסה לרצון הנעלם,
phrases.en: which is the hidden reason and the *chachma* that's in the *ratzon*, which is like the *geshmak*, the pleasure you get out of it.

phrases.he: ונקרא גם כן שכל הנעלם מכל רעיון
phrases.en: This is also called the *sechel* which is hidden from all thought,
or the wonders of *chachma*.

blocks.text: So it reaches the *etzem*, higher than the *mocha stima'a*, the source of intellect, which is the hidden reason and the *chachma* in the *ratzon*: the *geshmak* (relish), the pleasure in it. This is higher: the *etzem*'s own connection.

Hashem has a *bechira* (choice) in the Jews, higher than any reason: they are connected to Him just because He chose them. So even what makes no sense to the intellect can come out there: by the Torah a person sinned, and Hashem forgives him and connects to him anyway.

This is higher even than the source of the *sechel* in the *Keser*, called *sechel hane'elam mikol ra'ayon* (hidden from all thought) or *pla'os chachma* (the wonders of *chachma*).

phrases.en: Based on this,

phrases.he: כשאמר דאור אבא יונק ממזל כו',
phrases.en: when it says that the light of *chachma* receives, it sucks from the *mazal*,

phrases.he: הרי זה למעלה מחכמה סתימאה עצמה

blocks.text: So the light of *Abba* sucking from the *mazal* is higher than the *mocha stima'a* itself. It receives the few drops of liquid from the *mocha stima'a*, the *chachma* of *Keser*, but also from the *etzem* of the *Keser*, which forces the liquid down: really it receives from the *etzem*.

phrases.en: And this is why it says,
everything depends on a *mazal*,
even a *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal*,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת יחוד אבא ואמא למטה
phrases.en: which is the idea of the union of the *Abba* and *Ima* of *chachma* and *bina* below, your understanding:
the point of *chachma* in the *heichal* of *bina*.

blocks.text: This is why *hakol talui b'mazal*, everything depends on *mazal*, even a *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal* (the sanctuary): the union of *Abba* and *Ima* below, the point of *chachma* in the *heichal* of *bina*. Even understanding the Torah depends on the *mazal*.

There is more. The source of the *sechel* is in the *etzem*, and the *etzem* decides what will make sense and how the *chachma* will come out. The *mitzvos* come from Hashem's *ratzon*, higher than any reason, and His connection to the Jews from His *etzem*; the Torah makes sense only because He said it should. Revealing its source in the *mazal* reveals the level from which it could come out anyway.

This is what *Chassidus* does: it reveals the *etzem* of the *sechel*. That is why it explains the same thing in many, even opposite, ways and then shows how they all connect, something ordinary *sechel* would find ridiculous. It is a much higher *sechel*.

phrases.en: This is *sefer* and *sippur*.
That's called a *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal*.

blocks.text: This is *sefer* and *sippur*: the Torah is the *sefer* (book), *bina* the *sippur* (telling), both according to the *sofer* (scribe), the *etzem* that makes the *sechel*: a *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal*. Here *sechel* follows the *etzem* and its *bechira*: it makes sense because Hashem decided it should. And all the way down: He decided how Torah and *mitzvos* should be, and that is now the nature of the world.
A scientific study of the world would conclude that living by the Torah is the best thing *al pi sechel* (according to reason), but only because Hashem chose that it be so.

blocks.title: Why one plus one is two
blocks.text:
Even math makes sense only because G-d said it should. He made the world so that one plus one is two; had He made one plus one three, that would make sense, since He would have made your fingers that way. It is hard to imagine, because we know no other world.

Even here the source of one plus one being two is an *Echad* (one made of parts united): only because Hashem made *Echad* does it make sense to group separate things into a unit, and so there is math.

blocks.title: Three apples in a bowl
blocks.text:
Three apples in a bowl: counting them makes sense only because Hashem made this way of seeing separate things as part of a higher unity. Had He made the world only with the level of *Kadmon*, we would ask what you mean: an apple is an apple, and being near another apple does not make it two. "One plus one equals one plus one." Three is one and one and one.

Making them a unit of three, where they lose their individuality and are just a number, is only how our minds make generalities, seeing similar things as more of the same. Really each is its own unique thing.

blocks.title: No such thing as apples
blocks.text:
In a way it makes no sense to count them at all: this is one, and this is one, so what is ten? Some philosophies say there is no generality called apples, only individual apples, each different; on the level of *Kadmon* each is unique, with no connection to a generality.

A generality is a thing of *Echad*. Hashem made our minds see a unity among similar things, a mental or spiritual unity, not a physical one, though they are really separate and unique. Because He made us that way we can count.

sections.title: The arms of Arich Anpin: the middos of the will, mountains of darkness
sections.summary: Receiving from the *mazalos* is far higher than garbing the arms, *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*, and higher still than *Nehi*. The *middos* of the will are called mountains of darkness: like mountains the sun did not raise, they are feelings the intellect could never cause, rooted in the hidden *chachma*, the *ta'am kamus* that splits into *chesed* and *gevura*.

phrases.he: וזהו למעלה הרבה ממה שכתוב שאבא ואימא מלבישין לזרועות דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: And this way, where the *sechel* receives from the *mazalos* of *Arich*, is much, much higher than when the *sechel* garbs the *chesed* and *gevura*, the *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*, which is what we said is the arms of *Arich Anpin*,

phrases.he: ומכל שכן מבחינת נה''י דאריך אנפין שמלובשין באבא ואמא כו'
phrases.en: and for sure it's higher than when the *sechel* garbs the *Nehi* of *Arich Anpin*.

blocks.text: Three ways *Abba* and *Ima* receive from the *Keser*, from *Arich Anpin*. The first, by way of the *mazalos*, receives something of the very essence of the *Keser*. The hairs are hollow tubes that bring in a little liquid from the *mocha stima'a*, the *chachma* of *Arich Anpin*, the source of the *sechel*; but the hair itself reaches up to the skull, the actual *Keser* of *Arich*, where the seven lower *sefiros* of *Atik* shine. That revelation of *Atik* in the *sechel* is the level of *Chassidus*, of what we are doing now.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 27 opens by summing up lines 22-31 (the hairs and the mazalos) before it reads line 35.

blocks.text: "Hairs" means both the hairs of the beard and the head and what they correspond to inside the head. As the *Zohar* says, *is searos v'is searos*, there are hairs and there are hairs: the little tubes from the membrane into the brain are called hairs too.
blocks.outOfPlace: Part of class 27's opening summary of lines 22-31, before it reads line 35.

blocks.text: Now the next way. Receiving from the *mazalos* of *Arich* is much higher than when the *sechel* garbs its *Chagas*, its *chesed* and *gevura*, called its *zro'os* (arms), and surely than garbing its *Nehi*. So now, the *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.en: Being that it's known

phrases.he: שבחינת ז׳ תחתונים דאריך אנפין היינו רק בחינת המדות חג''ת כו'
phrases.en: the seven lower *sefiros* of *Arich Anpin*, which are the *middos*, *Chagas* and *Nehim*:

phrases.he: שנקרא יד הגדולה ויד החזקה כו',
phrases.en: those *Chagas*, the *chesed*, *gevura*, *tiferes*, are called the great hand, the strong hand, the uplifted hand.

phrases.he: ונקרא גם כן בזהר בשם טורי חשוכא
phrases.en: And these *middos* are also called in the *Zohar* the mountains of darkness.

blocks.text:
The seven lower *sefiros* of *Arich Anpin* are only the *middos*. Its *Chagas* are called the *yad hagedola*, the great hand, the *yad hachazaka*, the strong hand, and the *yad rama*, the uplifted hand.

They have a *heh*, "the" great, because this is the source: of the *Keser* only the *chitzoniyus* is revealed, not the *pnimiyus*, so the highest level revealed downward, an infinite revelation, is the *middos* of *Arich Anpin*. In the *Zohar* they are also called *turei chashocha*, the mountains of darkness; a *mashal* comes soon.

phrases.he: (כידוע במאמר דהאי איילתא אזלת לטורא חשוכא
phrases.en: As it's known about the teaching in the *Zohar* that says this gazelle runs to the mountain of darkness,
and from there it gets its food, it eats the grass there.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת עליית המלכות בחג"ת דאריך אנפין כו'
phrases.en: This is the idea of *Malchus*, which is called the gazelle, going up to receive from the level of *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*.
Like it says, the ark was lifted up, and it rested on Ararat,
in the seventh month, which is *Tishrei*,
and this is the idea of *Rosh Hashana*.

phrases.he: שעולה המלכות בהרי אררט טורי קרדניתא כו')
phrases.en: On *Rosh Hashana*, *Malchus* is lifted up to the mountain of Ararat, which is the mountain of darkness.

blocks.text: As the *Zohar* teaches, the gazelle runs to the mountains of darkness and finds its food there. The gazelle is *Malchus* (kingship), going up to receive from the *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*, its *middos*, the mountains of darkness.

As it says, the ark rested on Ararat, called the mountain of darkness, in the seventh month, *Tishrei*: *Rosh Hashana*. It actually rested on the seventeenth, but the ark lifted to Ararat is what happens on *Rosh Hashana*: *Malchus* rises to the *turei kardunisa*, the mountain of darkness, the *middos* of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.he: כמו הרים הגבוהים שאין אור השמש מאיר עליהם כו'
phrases.en: This is like a *mashal* of mountains that are so high that the light of the sun doesn't shine on them.

blocks.title: Mountains the sun could not raise
blocks.text: They are called mountains of darkness after a *mashal* of mountains so high the sun does not shine on them. Maybe a high mountain blocks the sun so a whole side is dark, or it is snow-capped because it is cold up there. But one explanation he saw elsewhere in *Chassidus*: the pull of the sun and moon, besides making tides, pulls up the ground and makes mountains. Certain very high mountains, like the Himalayas, would never exist from those forces; they are there only because Hashem made the world with them from the beginning of creation, whether simply made so or pushed higher and higher by tectonic plates. They are called higher than the sun: beyond its power to cause.

In the analogy the sun is the intellect. Some emotions your intellect can cause: if it tells you that you should feel a certain way, you will. But some feelings are natural, ingrained from birth, too strong for the intellect to cause, to the point of *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) that makes no sense, like a parent's love for a child, giving up his life for him. That love comes from the person's essence, not from the intellect.

That is called the *middos* of the *ratzon*: higher than a reason, simply the way Hashem made our nature. We like things a certain way, feel strongly about it, and almost nothing can change it. A person always has *bechira* (free choice), and with it he can change everything, but within his nature he will never change.

phrases.en: And these are the emotions within the *ratzon*,
which are higher than a revealed intellect and revealed reason.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן המדות שמצד שכל וטעם נקרא טורי דנהורא,
phrases.en: But the emotions that come about as a result of the intellect and the reason, those are called mountains of light,
because *chachma*, wisdom, the intellect, is called light.

blocks.text: These are the emotions within the *ratzon*, higher than revealed intellect and reason. Emotions caused by intellect and reason are called *turei d'nehora*, mountains of light: *chachma*, the intellect, is light, and the *middos* it shines into and causes are called light.

blocks.title: Where the earth protrudes
blocks.text: Why mountains? A mountain is where the Earth protrudes, and a person's *middos* are where his personality protrudes: the stronger you feel about something, the more you stick out there into the world and affect the people around you. What you do not feel strongly about is a little hill, or a flat plain where you do not care at all.

phrases.he: אבל המדות שברצון נקרא טורי חשוכא,
phrases.en: But the emotions within the *ratzon* are called mountains of darkness,
because these are the emotions that are hidden within the *ratzon*, which are higher than the intellect, and even than a conscious thought.

phrases.he: ושרשם מבחינת חכמה סתימאה הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: And their source is from the hidden *chachma*, not from the revealed *chachma*.
That's called the hidden source of *chachma*.

blocks.text: But the emotions within the *ratzon* are *turei chashocha*, mountains of darkness: hidden in the *ratzon*, above intellect and even conscious thought. *Middos* always come from *sechel*, these too, but from the hidden *chachma*, your subconscious *chachma*, the *chachma* of your *Keser*: its source in the *mocha stima'a*, spoken of with the *mazal*, called *taalumos chachma* (the hidden depths of wisdom).

phrases.en: This is like the inner reason for a *ratzon*,

phrases.he: שנחלק ממנו ב' קוין חסד וגבורה שברצון כו'
phrases.en: and so from here you have the two lines of *chesed* and *gevura* in the *ratzon*.

blocks.text: This is the *ta'am kamus* (hidden reason) of the *ratzon*. The *ta'am*, the reason for the will, is a *geshmak*; *ta'am* also means taste. Because a person enjoys things a certain way, his *ratzon* goes after one thing and not another, and that gives it form: the *chachma* of the *ratzon*. From it come inherent emotions, liking this and not that by nature, not for a reason; even when it makes no sense they supersede everything, like a parent's love for a child over every rational consideration.
From this reason for the *ratzon* it already divides into lines: *chesed* and *gevura* in the *ratzon*, a *sechel* that leans to *chesed* and one that leans to *gevura*, whether you like it or not.

sections.title: Abba and Ima garb the arms: the bribe of the will, and the intellect as its puppet
sections.summary: When *chachma* and *bina* garb the *chesed* and *gevura* of *Arich Anpin*, the intellect only rationalizes a love or bias in the will, like a puppet on the arms. A bribe blinds the eyes of the wise: Rabbi Yishmael, given his own basket of fruit a day early, found his mind arguing for the man. True *sechel* needs the level of the *mazalos*.

phrases.en: And this is why it says

phrases.he: דאבא ואמא מלבישין לזרועות חסד וגבורה דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: that the *Abba* and *Ima*, the *chachma* and *bina*, garb or clothe the arms of *Arich Anpin*, which represents the *chesed* and *gevura* of *Arich Anpin*.

blocks.text: That is why *Abba* and *Ima*, *chachma* and *bina*, garb the arms of *Arich Anpin*, its *chesed* and *gevura*: the level where your intellect rests on your essential desires, your *ratzon*, your bias. You love your child, so your intellect looks for the good in him and cannot see bad; self-love covers your own faults. The intellect is only rationalizing these *middos*.

So too when a person feels very strongly about a belief and his intellect tries to rationalize it: it is not really intellect but a belief or emotion higher than intellect, explained in order to convince, and not open for debate.

You see it with missionaries, with political groups, with anybody who campaigns for a belief he feels strongly about. He tries to convince you rationally, but defeat his argument and he still believes, because he believes above the intellect. This is neither good nor bad, "just the way people work," and anyone will be like this some of the time.

sensitivity.reason: Names missionaries and political groups as people who argue from a belief they will not give up even when their argument is defeated.
sensitivity.publishable: You see it with anybody who campaigns for a belief he feels strongly about. He tries to convince you rationally, but defeat his argument and he still believes, because he believes above the intellect. This is neither good nor bad, "just the way people work," and anyone will be like this some of the time.

blocks.text: To come out with a true *sechel* you have to reach the first level, all the way up into the source. At this level you will come up with very smart things, but built on what you already believe: true maybe, but not the full truth.

In holiness too: *Beis Shammai* and *Beis Hillel* *paskened* partly from their source, one leaning to *chesed* and one to *gevura*, and their intellect saw things that way. *Halacha* has to reach higher, into the source above *chesed* and *gevura*, the *mazalos*, to see where the *hachra'a* is.

A *maamar* or two in *Samech Vav* explain *eilu v'eilu divrei Elokim chaim* (these and these are the words of the living G-d): both true, but not the whole truth. Real truth comes not from *Elokim* but from *Havaya*, which reaches the essence, the level of the *mazalos*; from there comes the *halacha*, the power to decide for one side, here like *Beis Hillel*.

Whenever someone in a debate has a natural leaning, he just feels he is right and tries to make you see what he feels: the intellect explaining what he inherently feels. To find the truth you have to reach the *mazalos*, where you see both sides and the inner truth behind both, and can connect them. Speaking to people at the lower level is very frustrating; arguing the other side will not really work.

That is why it is like puppets: the arms go into *chachma* and *bina* and move them as they want, and the intellect is "just a mask, a front for the *ratzon*." With the *mazalos* the intellect is a front too, but you are not biased: you see the inner truth and bring the intellect out however you choose to explain it, transparent to what is behind it, a true *sechel*. That is the level of Torah, and of *Chassidus* in particular.

phrases.en: Like we see

phrases.he: שמחמת מדת החסד ואהבה רבה שברצון,
phrases.en: that when a person has an essential desire of *chesed* and *ahava* in their *ratzon*, this infinite love in their *ratzon*,

phrases.he: נמצא שרש לשכל וטעם לזכות ולחסד
phrases.en: this will cause them to have an intellect and a reason for merit and for kindness and for good.

blocks.text: As we see: an essential desire of *chesed* and *ahava* (love) in the *ratzon*, an infinite love, gives a person an intellect and a reason for merit, for kindness and for good.

phrases.en: Like a bribe: a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise.

phrases.he: שמחמת השוחד שיש לו אהבה ברצון
ממציא טענה ומטעה כח שכלו מחוב לזכות
phrases.en: So this will bring out a *ta'ana*, and it will twist his intellect from guilt to innocence.

blocks.text: That is *shochad*: a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise, and the love in your *ratzon* bribes your *sechel*. Give a person money and his desire for it, above the *sechel*, reaches his *etzem hanefesh* (the essence of the soul), brings out a *ta'ana* (an argument) and twists his intellect from guilt to innocence. However holy you are, you cannot stop it: connect your *sechel* to a bribe and you will be biased.

phrases.he: וכמו ר׳ ישמעאל שלקח כלכלה דפירי, אמר אי בעי טעין הכי כו'

blocks.title: Rabbi Yishmael's basket of fruit
blocks.text:
*Bava Basra* has a run of stories showing how far a bribe reaches: someone did a sage a small favor on the day of his court case, and the sage counted it a bribe and would not judge him.

The most extreme is Rabbi Yishmael. His sharecropper brought him a basket of fruit every Friday, as part of their deal. Once, with a court case pending, the man came a day early, on Thursday, with the basket. It was Rabbi Yishmael's own fruit, only a day early, but he called it a bribe and passed the case to another judge. Sitting in the *beis midrash* while they judged it, he caught himself thinking the whole time of the arguments the man should be making. He told the story to show how strong a bribe is: for so small a favor, he was inextricably biased toward the man.

phrases.he: נמצא המדות חסד וגבורה מלובשים בפנימית דאבא ואמא,
phrases.en: So it comes out that the *middos* of *chesed* and *gevura* of the *Keser* go into the *pnimiyus* of the *sechel*, *chachma* and *bina*,

phrases.he: ובחינת אבא ואמא מלבישים אותן מבחוץ
phrases.en: and now *chachma* and *bina* are just like masks or puppets that surround them on the outside.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אני בינה לי גבורה
phrases.en: Like it says, "I am *bina*; in me is *gevura*."

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים ודי למבין
phrases.en: Like it says in *Etz Chaim*, and this is enough to understand.

blocks.text: So the *middos* of *chesed* and *gevura* of the *Keser* go into the *pnimiyus* (inner part) of the *sechel*, and *chachma* and *bina* are masks or puppets around them, an outer garment over the *ratzon*. It is really a *ratzon*, not a *sechel*: really the bribe, so to speak.

As it says, "I am *bina*; in me is *gevura*" of *Arich Anpin*. The verse is read both ways, *gevura* in *bina* and *gevura* from *bina*; here, the *gevura* of *Arich Anpin* is hidden inside *bina*. As *Etz Chaim* says, *v'dai l'mevin* (enough for one who understands). That is the second level: an inherent desire twists the intellect to fit what the person feels.

sections.title: The lowest way: netzach and hod of Arich Anpin, and the yesod of Arich and of Zeir Anpin
sections.summary: Lowest of all, the intellect receives from *netzach* and *hod* of *Arich Anpin*, which carry out *chesed* and *gevura*: the everyday intellect, running on axioms it does not question, though still unlimited because it serves the will. The *yesod* of *Arich Anpin* is the abundant good, a cedar valued for itself; the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* is small, a palm kept for its fruit, down to the hyssop in the wall.

phrases.en: And then as the light descends lower,

phrases.he: אין מוחין דחכמה ובינה דאצילות מקבלים רק מבחינת נצח והוד דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: there's an even lower level, where the intellect only receives from the *netzach* and *hod* of *Arich Anpin*,

phrases.he: שהוא הבאת השפע דחסד וגבורה למטה
phrases.en: which *netzach* and *hod* just bring out the *chesed* and *gevura* to actuality; they're bringing it down.

phrases.he: כמו נצח והוד שנקרא מאזני צדק בכמה מקומות,
phrases.en: Like *netzach* and *hod*, which are called the scales of justice; on every level they're called the scales of justice.

phrases.he: גם למטה במדות שמצד אור השכל
phrases.en: This is true also in the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*, which are under the *sechel*.

blocks.text: As the light descends, a still lower level: the intellect receives only from the *netzach* and *hod* (victory and acknowledgement) of *Arich Anpin*, which bring *chesed* and *gevura* down into action. On every level they are called *moznei tzedek*, the scales of justice, also in the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance), below the *sechel*: *netzach* and *hod* always bring the flow down.

Once you know what is good and what is bad, you must work out how to carry the ruling out in a particular case: weigh what is just here, the sentence as opposed to the verdict. Punish him or reward him, and how? Give, or hold back?

phrases.he: רק במדות שברצון שנקרא אריכות דאנפין,
phrases.en: The only difference is that when it's in the *middos* of the *ratzon*, the *middos* of *Keser*, there it's called *Arich Anpin*, it's called a big face.
At that level, *netzach* and *hod* are not limited,
just like the *ratzon* itself,
which is not limited.

phrases.he: על כן גם בחינת נצח והוד

phrases.en: They're also unlimited.

blocks.text: The only difference: in the *middos* of the *ratzon*, of *Keser*, it is *Arich Anpin*, a big face, mature, infinite *middos*, and there *netzach* and *hod* are unlimited like the *ratzon* itself. In *Arich Anpin* you do not want a good job, you want infinite money; not a nice house, but a huge palace. The love and fear of *Chagas* there are infinite, essential *middos*, and so is the *Nehi*.

There *netzach* and *hod* too are unlimited. A person's essential love for his family makes him work to provide their food, clothing and shelter. Coming from an essential desire, the application, that he loves his family and so must provide for them, is essential too, and it will never stop.

When the intellect receives from this *netzach* and *hod*, it is already normal intellect, the way yours works on a regular day. You are not thinking about the inner truth behind things, the *mazalos*, up to *Chabad* and the *Keser* above it, nor about your inner beliefs, values and morals, the *Chagas*. Those, with your worldview and nature, are already set; you just apply them: go to work, figure out how to drive there and do your job, get the groceries, your day-to-day.

That is regular intellect. In a way it is honest, since you are not so partial, but you are not looking into the truth of things at all. You assume the whole system, all the axioms, and work from there. To get to the truth of an idea you have to question back to the original axioms, check them and build from there; without digging into the source you will never find it. Once it is all set up, "the intellect just runs on autopilot."

phrases.en: As it's known, that when it says, "Remember your abundant goodness,"
that's the idea of *yesod* of *Arich Anpin*.
And see also that it says, "Your great goodness," and the like.

phrases.he: וכן אם יגאלך טוב, ורב טוב לבית ישראל וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: It says, if you will bestow goodness, and abundant goodness to the House of Israel.

blocks.text: As is known, *zecher rav tuvcha*, "Remember Your abundant goodness," is the *yesod* of *Arich Anpin*: *tov* (good) is *yesod*, as will be explained, and *rav tuvcha*, Your great, infinite goodness, is the *yesod* of *Arich Anpin*, where G-d connects to us infinitely and always wants to give to us, no matter what. So too "abundant goodness to the House of Israel": two levels, the regular *tov* of *Zeir Anpin* and the *rav tov* of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בחינת יסוד זעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: But the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*:
those are the emotions that come only based on a reason; they're coming out from the intellect.
Those are very small, very immature.

blocks.text: But the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* is the *middos* born from *bina*, emotions that come only from a reason, very small and immature: you are connected only for a reason, and when the reason goes, you stop.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין צדיק כתמר, שזהו בחינת יסוד זעיר אנפין
כארז בלבנון ישגה, בבחינת אין סוף,
שהוא ביסוד עתיק יומין ואריך אנפין
phrases.en: That's the *yesod* of *Atik* and *Arich*.

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere on *tzaddik katamar yifrach, k'erez balevanon yisgeh*, the *tzaddik* will flourish like a palm, he will grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon: the palm is the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, the cedar the infinite *yesod* of *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* (where the text, he says, should read *Ein Sof*). A *tzaddik*, who represents *yesod*, starts out like a date palm and becomes a cedar.

blocks.title: The date palm
blocks.text: A date palm is for its fruit; once it stops giving fruit it is worthless, not even good wood. That is a person who grows and works only for a reason, connected only for the fruit, like a kid learning for candy or a reward: the small *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*.

blocks.title: The cedar
blocks.text: The *yesod* of *Arich Anpin* is doing it with an inherent integrity, because you want to: the cedar, which has no fruit but valuable wood. You do it because the thing itself is valuable, a good deed because it is right, not for a reward. So too Torah and *mitzvos* done to connect to Hashem: *s'char mitzva mitzva* (the reward of a *mitzva* is the *mitzva*). Connecting to Hashem is the reward; you need no separate *Olam Haba*, *Gan Eden*, money or blessings. "The fruit is the thing itself."

And it is in *Levanon*, *lamed-beis nun*: the source of *chachma* and *bina*, the thirty-two paths of *chachma* and the fiftieth gate of *bina*, which reach up to the *etzem* and not only to what comes out of it. Appreciating the thing itself is a cedar in Lebanon.

phrases.en: And similarly, like it says about *Shlomo HaMelech*,

phrases.he: וידבר מן הארז אשר בלבנון עד האזוב,
phrases.en: he spoke about the cedar tree that's in Lebanon, all the way to the weed that grows out of the wall,

phrases.he: בחינת קטנות יסוד זעיר אנפין במלכות, שנקרא קיר כו'

blocks.text: So too *Shlomo HaMelech*, King Solomon, the wisest man, spoke of all plants, from the cedar in Lebanon to the weed that grows out of the wall: from the greatest tree to the smallest weed. He explained the actual plants, but also *yesod*, which is like a plant: the ground is *Malchus*, and the tree grows out of it and stays connected to it, like the *middos* at the level of *yesod*, connected to *Malchus*.

The cedar in Lebanon is the *yesod* of *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*, and he went all the way down to the smallest *yesod*, of *Zeir Anpin*, growing out of *Malchus*, the *kir*, the wall: a wall is like *Malchus* because it is *batel* (nullified), just an inanimate thing. Like the weeds growing out of the cracks in the *Kosel*.

phrases.he: (וכידוע בכוונות דאמן יהא שמיא רבא מברך
phrases.en: And this is the idea when we *daven* and we say *Amen yehei shmei rabba mevarach*: what are we saying?
*Shmei*, your name, has the same *gematria* as *ratzon*, desire.

phrases.he: ושמו הגדול בבחינת יסוד ומלכות דאריך
phrases.en: *Shmei rabba*, your great name, the big name: that's the *yesod* and the *Malchus* of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.he: שיהיה מבורך באבא ואמא וזעיר אנפין ונוקבא כו'
phrases.en: We're saying that it should be drawn down into the *sechel*, the *Abba* and *Ima*, and then *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*.
That the right should overpower the left.

phrases.he: וכמו ובטובך הגדול ישוב כו' ודי למבין)
phrases.en: Like we say, "In Your abundant goodness return us."

blocks.text: In the *kavanos* (mystical intentions) of *Amen yehei shmei rabba mevarach*, "may Your great name be blessed": *shmei*, Your name, has the *gematria* (numerical value) of *ratzon*, desire. *Shmei rabba*, the great name, is the *yesod* and *Malchus* of *Arich Anpin*: *Malchus* is the *shem* (name), connected to *Zeir Anpin* through *yesod*. We ask that it be drawn down into *Abba* and *Ima*, then *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, *l'agbara yemina al smala*, the right overpowering the left: that Hashem's essential connection to the Jews be revealed and He have mercy on us. As we say, "In Your abundant goodness return us."

The main request is for *Moshiach*: as explained before, he thinks, *shmei rabba* reaches the *ratzon kadum* (the primordial will), the will for *Moshiach*. Here the stress is that it is brought out into *Abba* and *Ima* and *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*: *middos* that follow the essential *ratzon* never change, so whether we deserve it or not, Hashem will always give us good. Even this lowest level of intellect follows the *ratzon*.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the three ways *Abba* and *Ima* receive from *Arich Anpin*, and which is highest?
How does the stick figure show the way *chachma* shines into *bina*?
What are the *mazalos* in the brain, and why do the first six bring pleasure and the last six intellect?
Why is calling the Torah *novlos chachma shel maala* a praise, and what general rule does it show?
Why are the *middos* of the will called mountains of darkness, and how does the story of Rabbi Yishmael show what happens when the intellect garbs them?
What is the difference between the date palm and the cedar in Lebanon?

notes.text: Phrases with no English: lines suoryrfr (last phrase), cqw7uder, koj7xarm, yvpfaoke, qbbgzu55, i6bu2xrz (middle phrase), 3dlvoc6x (first phrase), wqifdwes, pvasksv4 (first phrase), fxelsse4 (last phrase). He reads them in Hebrew and goes straight into explanation or a story.

Line 4: he cites chapter 21 for chesed of Atik Yomin becoming the sechel and gevura of Atik Yomin becoming mocha stima'a (24 w495-517). The chapter itself says only "as mentioned above"; the block keeps his reference.

The eighth mazal is heard as both ונצר and ונוצר; the chapter spells ונוצר. The middle mazal he names as v'emes (24 w2053). He says the first seven mazalos do not relate to sechel, having said the first six are pleasure and the seventh the intermediary; the blocks keep both.
Line 23: he renders "higher than the inner body of the mocha stima'a" as "higher than this liquid", since the liquid is the mocha stima'a in his explanation; the phrase keeps his words.

The question "does whoever says stupid things is very smart?" is not heard; he answers "Well, no" (25 w1493) and "Regular people's... No" (25 w1623) as if to an objection, perhaps from a listener off the tape. Written as askedBy teacher, as the series notes say no student is heard.
"Right, yeah, math only makes sense" (26 w1123) also sounds like an answer to a remark not on the tape; the digression keeps it as he said it.

Sources as he gives them: stories about bribes in Bava Basra, Rabbi Yishmael and the basket of fruit (the story is in Kesubos 105b); a maamar or a couple of maamarim in Samech Vav on eilu v'eilu, and Hemshech Samech Vav for the Rav afraid to pasken. A reviewer may want to check these.
Line 60: the chapter has אם יגאלך טוב; he reads יגמלך and translates "if you will bestow goodness". The phrase keeps his English.
Line 64: he says the text "is supposed to read Ein Sof" (29 w1190-1197); the chapter file already reads בבחינת אין סוף.
Class 27's opening summary (w0-261) recaps lines 22-31; it is placed under line 35's passage, where the class resumes, with outOfPlace, so that the opening plays before the reading of line 35.

Sensitivity: one flag, his naming of missionaries and political groups as arguing past reason (28 w277-416). Left unflagged: Torah as higher than reason and science ("math only makes sense because G-d said"), his remarks that modern science does not yet understand the brain, and the brain physiology he gives from Torah sources, which he himself frames as not correlated to medicine.

Class 26 w1354: "if G-d would have made the world only with like קדמוני" is the machine's hearing; the block writes *Kadmon*, unglossed. What level he names here (Adam Kadmon, or something else) could not be told from the transcript; a reviewer should listen.

Line 40, the mountains the sun could not raise (27 w907-1164): he credits the sun-and-moon explanation to "another place in Chassidus"; the alternative of tectonic plates pushing up the Himalayas follows in his own words with "maybe", and the block keeps it as his open aside rather than the source's.
